title: AI Selloff Tests Investor Confidence
summary: Ritholtz Wealth Management Chairman and Chief Investment Officer Barry Ritholtz tells Bloomberg This Weekend that AI remains a transformational technology, but investors face a difficult task determining which companies will ultimately emerge as winners and losers. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Ritholtz discusses CoreWeave’s selloff, concerns about AI financing and valuations, and the challenges facing Tesla as competition in electric vehicles intensifies. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Zelenskyy Says Starlink Restrictions on Ukraine Look Deliberate
summary: Restrictions on Ukraine’s military use of SpaceX’s Starlink system appear to be deliberate and not the result of any technical problems, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Saturday.

title: The EV Bust Creating a New Battery Boom
summary: Factories built to supply America’s electric-vehicle boom are getting a second life making batteries for the power grid.  As EV demand weakens and electricity demand from data centers and new factories strengthens, battery makers are shifting toward stationary storage, but the new market still relies on federal incentives and a supply chain that remains partly dependent on China. The shift is visible at TransGrid’s Atlas projects in Arizona, where the contractor Qcells is using LG Energy Solution’s US-made battery cells. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: David Byrne Explains How Forgotten Ideas Come Back to Life
summary: History is littered with ideas that have been tossed aside, only for them to gain relevance at some later date. Think of Moby-Dick: forgotten in Melville's time, but now regarded as the great American novel. Or the work of economist Hyman Minsky, which became influential a decade after his death, when the 2008 financial crisis made “the Minsky Moment” a mainstream term. These are just a couple of the things we talk about with the legendary musician David Byrne on today's podcast. Byrne's new book, Sleeping Beauties: Why Good Ideas Go Dormant and How They Wake Up, looks to categorize numerous “sleeping beauties” — ideas that were lost but then rediscovered. Besides Melville and Minsky, we also talk about the lost Roman recipe for concrete and we get into Byrne's thoughts on how to write a song and his own experience of having his music rediscovered by a new generation. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Reliance Pushes Back After Musk Questioned Starlink India Delay
summary: Reliance Industries Ltd., led by billionaire Mukesh Ambani, pushed back against suggestions that it is trying to keep Elon Musk’s Starlink Inc. out of India, saying its own satellite venture is still awaiting regulatory clearances.

title: Arrested OpenAI Engineer Seeks Bail, Denies Planning to Flee
summary: The OpenAI software engineer charged with using a hidden recording device in one of the company’s offices asked to be freed from custody and denied his purchase of a one-way plane ticket to his native Saudi Arabia was part of a plan to flee US justice.

title: Nvidia Partner GMI Cloud Calls CoreWeave 15% Yield ‘Insane’
summary: The founder of a cloud computing company with a similar business model to CoreWeave Inc. said the 15% yield on the latter’s bonds is “insane,” compared with the roughly 3.45% rate his company secured on a recent Taiwan dollar loan.

title: AI Music Deals Are Happening, But How Artists Will Be Paid Remains a Mystery
summary: How exactly AI money will flow through the music industry remains ambiguous

title: Anthropic Pitches AI Safety Bill to Lawmakers
summary: Anthropic PBC has presented its own draft bill to US lawmakers with a plan for regulating artificial intelligence safety and security, in a moment of heightened concern about the potential risks of the rapidly advancing technology.

title: Wall Street Week | America’s Relationship Woes, Battery Pivot, Farmers’ Fed Warning
summary:
This week, global and business leaders gathered in New Delhi for the Bloomberg New Economy Forum to discuss how the world is redrawing supply chains and investment plans in the face of geopolitical risks. And, in her new book former Canadian deputy prime minister Chrystia Freeland and Former Treasury Secretary Yellen say that the US needs stronger economic ties with its allies. Plus, can storage technologies rescue battery factories built in the hopes of stronger EV adoption? Later, as inflation picks up in the US, the heartland feels the effects more severely.
 (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Apple Says iPhone Duo Demand Extraordinary After Delivery Delays
summary: Apple Inc. said demand for the new iPhone Duo has been “nothing short of extraordinary” after shipping estimates slipped to the end of January of next year just minutes after pre-orders opened on Friday.

title: JP Morgan Strategist on AI Jitters, Investing Outlook
summary: Jordan Jackson, JPMorgan Asset Management Global Market Strategist, discusses whether earnings growth may be nearing a peak even if results are not worsening. Jackson agrees that third-quarter results are expected to be strong, with forecasts calling for about 27% to 28% year-over-year earnings growth. He speaks with Romaine Bostick & Kristine Aquino on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: OpenAI Poaches Another SpaceX Sales Lead Focused on AI
summary: OpenAI has hired SpaceX’s Graham Seamans to lead sales for the firm’s cybersecurity business, the latest in a string of hires from Elon Musk’s artificial intelligence venture.

title: CoreWeave Stock Wipeout Exposes Divide Between AI Fear and Greed
summary: CoreWeave Inc. has become caught in a tug of war between investors who see rising bond yields as a potential rally killer for the AI trade and those who think demand for computing power will make those concerns seem passe before long.

title: Apple Names Meta Veteran as Litigation Chief in Legal Team Shake-Up
summary: Apple Inc. has tapped a longtime Meta Platforms Inc. executive as its new litigation chief, bolstering its legal team at a time when the iPhone maker faces a growing array of lawsuits.

title: Anthropic Signs First Data-Center Deal in Canada With EverWind
summary: Anthropic PBC signed its first data-center lease in Canada, agreeing to buy capacity at a new project that’s worth more than C$10 billion ($7.1 billion) in the eastern province of Nova Scotia.

title: Thomas Hoenig on Rate Hikes, Inflation Outlook
summary: Thomas Hoenig said Kevin Warsh’s refusal to signal the Fed’s next move was appropriate and gives policymakers flexibility ahead of the late-October meeting. Hoenig noted that inflation has risen and could climb further, citing energy costs and their spillover into core prices. He speaks with Romaine Bostick & Kristine Aquino on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Janus Henderson CEO on Going Private, M&A Deals
summary: Janus Henderson CEO Ali Dibadj said the firm is energized by its move to private ownership and is using the flexibility to invest in people, technology including AI, new products and client service. He said quarterly earnings pressures had constrained those investments, despite the firm’s growth as a public company. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Financing The AI Boom: Masters in Business with Bob Michele
summary: Barry speaks with Bob Michele, CIO and Head of Global Fixed Income, Currency, and Commodities at JPMorgan. They discuss Bob's unconventional start at the University of Pennsylvania, the differences between the science of bonds and the art of equities, and whether the US is heading toward a recession. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: EM Stocks, FX Gain on Bets Fed Will Hold Rates This Month
summary: Gauges of emerging-market currencies and stocks gained on Friday as the greenback extended losses and a selloff in shares related to artificial intelligence abated in Asia.
